clue.text: Where you'll find man in the street champions album newly released

definitions.text: Where you'll find man in the street

indicators.note: something newly released comes out in a fresh form, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sports team's victorious record has just come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly released' rearranges CHAMPIONS ALBUM. The 'man on the Clapham omnibus' is the English legal figure of the ordinary reasonable person; Clapham is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the ordinary reasonable person of English law is pictured riding a bus through Clapham, so that vehicle is where the typical citizen sits.

clue.text: Incompetent pirate may be getting better and ready to encompass end of sea dog on shallow water

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the money word goes round the letter picked next

parts.note: tin is slang for money, as is 'the ready'

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from sea

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
a wash is a stretch of shallow water, as in the Wash in eastern England

explanation.surface: A seafaring rogue recovers and prepares to circle the ship's dog in the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is a British slang word for cash, here TIN; 'end of sea' gives A, placed inside it to make TAIN. Captain Pugwash is a bumbling pirate from a long-running British children's cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon buccaneer of British children's television is famously hopeless, always rescued by his cabin boy.

clue.text: Brought up nonsense about performer

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up letters reads them from bottom to top, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone raised on nonsense talks about a stage player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' turns ROTCA round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stage or screen player is a performer by trade.

clue.text: Extra circle in dance — suggestion for the hula?

indicators.note: in places the circle within the dance word

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
a circle looks like the letter O, and an extra one is added

explanation.surface: A dancer adds another twirl, perhaps with a hula move in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: HOP already has an O; the 'extra' one sits beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the phrase 'hula ___', the toy ring swung round the waist, so it is the natural follow-on to hula.

clue.text: Former star of American musicals in a main role?

definitions.meaning: Ethel ... was a Broadway star of shows such as Gypsy and Annie Get Your Gun
the main is the open sea, so this is a part played by a sea-dwelling man with a fish's tail

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is an old word for the high sea, not the leading part it seems to mean.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of the Broadway singer Ethel; the other is the male counterpart of a mermaid, living in the ocean.

clue.text: See 1
Nothing in London and Paris ahead of endless discussion about China?

indicators.note: ahead of places the first pieces before what follows

parts.note: in English, nothing is zero, the letter O
in Paris, French for nothing is rien

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: talk means discussion

explanation.surface: A European city pair says nothing before an unfinished chat on China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' does duty for both cities: English O and French RIEN. 'endless' trims TALK to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the East, of which China is the prime example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Onion place — possibly descriptive of France at some time

definitions.text: descriptive of France at some time

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A spot where onions grow could stand for France in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONION PLACE. The definition is fair because France under Bonaparte was a Napoleonic state.
explanation.definitionFit: France under the emperor Bonaparte in the early nineteenth century could be called by this adjective.

clue.text: Heralding British taking on US city planning policy?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
zoning is the town-planning policy of assigning land to uses

explanation.surface: A Briton adopting an American city's land-use rules is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: To blazon is to proclaim publicly, as a herald does; the word also describes heraldic arms.

clue.text: Electric current, in various places, brings about wonders on screen

indicators.note: in places the current letter within the rearranged word
various suggests a mixed, assorted arrangement of the letters

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
to effect is to bring about

explanation.surface: Electricity running through many spots produces cinematic marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges PLACES as SPECAL; 'in' puts I inside to give the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Film trickery, physical or digital, that creates impossible sights for audiences watching a cinema or TV picture.

clue.text: Recalled best serve, right one for various things

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: top means best
to pour a drink is to serve it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A top tennis serve was remembered, one correct option among several.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns TOP into POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a medley or miscellany, from the scented mix of dried petals.

clue.text: Town, perhaps, left in the grip of progress

indicators.note: held in the grip of means enclosed by the other word

parts.note: pace is rate of progress

explanation.surface: A town is left behind by development.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is one kind of locality, a definition by example marked by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Account in connection with amount of land

parts.note: re means concerning, in connection with

explanation.surface: A bookkeeping entry relating to a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of area, 4,840 square yards, used for farms and estates.

clue.text: Clergyman, one accepting King's mistress as an exotic dish

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the mistress goes inside

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral's clergy
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A churchman takes in a royal lover as something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: NELL Gwyn, an actress, was Charles II's best-known mistress; she sits inside CANONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian pasta tubes stuffed and baked, a foreign dish to the British table.

clue.text: Artist showing a lot of daring around rocks, taking end of chisel to one

indicators.note: around places the trimmed word round the next piece
a lot of the word means most of it, the final letter dropped

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve
ice is 'rocks', as in a drink on the rocks

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sculptor shows nerve among rocks, applying a chisel to a block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daring' is British slang 'bottle' (nerve), and 'a lot of' drops its last letter; 'rocks' means ice, as in a drink on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandro Botticelli was the Florentine Renaissance painter of The Birth of Venus.

clue.text: Scientist's recent quality falling short

definitions.note: read as 'scientist is', the 's linking to the wordplay

parts.note: new means recent

indicators.note: falling short drops the final letter

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: A researcher's new work is not quite up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' trims TONE to TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, the English physicist who framed the laws of motion and gravity.

clue.text: Avian features around turbulent lake? They're not too strong

indicators.note: around puts the bird parts about the mixed letters

parts.note: wings are what birds have

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so the letters are stirred

explanation.surface: Birds on a stormy lake are not robust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' stirs only the lake's four letters, which 'around' puts inside the bird parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble people lacking physical strength or force of character.

clue.text: Chap I encountered in examination of nobleman's land

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: encountered in means found within, placing I inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A man met in a viva relating to a lord's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encountered in' puts I inside ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a manor, the estate held by a lord in feudal England.

clue.text: Worried after reversal of gun control

indicators.note: after places the worried word behind the gun
reversal of turns the weapon word back to front

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Anxious after a U-turn on firearms legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal of' turns the German pistol round; 'Worried' works through the idiom 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to govern or control by rules.

clue.text: One chattering should be quiet with snake adjacent

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical instruction for quiet
a rattler is a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: A chatterbox ought to hush when a rattlesnake is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prattles talks on in a childish or trivial way.

clue.text: See 1
Judge recording to be without opening catchy tune

indicators.note: without opening removes the first letter

parts.note: a single is a recorded song released alone

explanation.surface: A judge says a song lacking an intro is merely a catchy ditty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' strips the S from SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short memorable tune, especially one used in advertising.

clue.text: See 8
Key argument in legal document

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A crucial dispute inside a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed or bond held by a third party until a condition is met.

clue.text: Government absolutely should embrace Liberal links

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: of course means absolutely, certainly

explanation.surface: The government certainly ought to welcome Liberal ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should embrace' puts L inside GOFCOURSE, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Links is a golf course, strictly a seaside one on sandy ground.

clue.text: Remove fellows attending party

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the fellows sit beside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
FF is short for fellows

explanation.surface: Throwing out the men who went to the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off, as a hat; to doff is to remove clothing.

clue.text: Unusual for us, absorbing time and energy

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: something for us is ours, belonging to us
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something odd for us takes up our time and effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means eccentric, beyond the bounds of convention.

clue.text: Help half of a group of characters

indicators.note: half of keeps four of the eight letters, dropping the front half

parts.note: the alphabet is a set of letters, or characters

explanation.surface: Assist half a cast of characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the back half of ALPHABET.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to aid or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Cancel plant after one American withdraws

indicators.note: withdraws takes the letter out of the word

parts.note: an annual is a plant that lives one year
A is short for American

explanation.surface: An order for a plant is cancelled when a US buyer pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdraws' removes one A from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, to cancel a law or a marriage.

clue.text: A reptile about to strike — I must be agile

indicators.note: about places the reptile around the next word

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile
to bat is to strike, as a ball

explanation.surface: A crocodile is poised to lunge, so I must be nimble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the reptile round both the striking word and I, not the striking word alone; 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic means nimble and supple, like a circus tumbler.

clue.text: Enlist who is set to work in support for the opposition?

definitions.note: describes a person who, though called by one side in a trial, ends up backing the other

indicators.note: set to work, the letters are put through a process that rearranges them

explanation.surface: Recruit someone ready to labour for the rival side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges ENLIST WHO IS SET. The definition is cryptic: a court figure called by one side who helps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, a person called to give evidence who turns out adverse to the party that called them, effectively aiding the other side.

clue.text: See 28
